svg.title: Ventricular surfaces in evaginated and everted forebrains, and early zebrafish telencephalic development
svg.desc: Panel A compares simplified transverse sections of an evaginated tetrapod telencephalon, in which each hemisphere surrounds an internal ventricle, and an everted teleost telencephalon, in which the ventricular surface lies on the upper surface of the hemispheres beneath a thin tela choroidea, with a narrow ventricular space between them. Panel B shows early zebrafish development in two steps. First, dorsal views at 18 and 22 hours post-fertilization show the anterior intraencephalic sulcus opening between telencephalon and diencephalon, creating a posterior telencephalic wall and displacing the posterior telencephalon laterally. Second, parasagittal and dorsal views at 2 and 5 days post-fertilization show the posterior ventricular wall bulging up and back while the tela choroidea and the ventricular surface beneath it extend forward over the upper surface of the telencephalon behind the olfactory bulbs. A small transverse section shows the everted arrangement at 5 days. The sequence is early development and not a complete map of adult pallial territories.

g.text: A: Two arrangements of the ventricular surface
hpf, hours post-fertilization; dpf, days post-fertilization
